Answer: B
Reason: The ultrasound images demonstrate a multicystic lesion in the fetal thorax (indicated by arrows) with color Doppler showing a systemic feeding vessel, characteristic of a bronchopulmonary sequestration or CPAM. Such lesions typically arise in the lower or middle lobes and, when large enough to be symptomatic or clearly visible with mass effect as implied by the options, cause mediastinal shift (displacing the heart to the contralateral/left side) and elevation of the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm due to mass effect. Option B is the only choice that correctly describes this mass-effect relationship (heart displacement and diaphragm elevation).
